one_liner: Notion has a broad REST API with free self-serve internal tokens, PATs and public OAuth, plus an official hosted MCP server; ready to build.
auth_notes: Public connections use OAuth 2.0 authorization code. Internal connection tokens and personal access tokens are static bearer tokens. Business/Enterprise plans restrict PAT creation by default.
access_notes: Integrations can be created on any plan including Free (third-party source). PATs are self-serve from the Developer portal; on Business/Enterprise a workspace owner must enable creation.
blocker_notes: No meaningful blocker; a free personal workspace provides owner rights for internal connections and PATs.

evidence.quote: personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
There’s no OAuth flow to implement — you get a token immediately when you create the connection, and you use that same token for every API request.
A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.
You can create an integration on any of the four plans, so your plan tier doesn't restrict your ability to build integrations
**Notion MCP** (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`) is our hosted, actively maintained server.
Notion provides a hosted [MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/introduction) server that lets MCP clients work with Notion workspaces.
